title.title: Kaplansky's quasitraces are not traces
title.subtitle: Claim: a separable unital C*-algebra with 2-quasitraces but no tracial state

beats.text: A 2-quasitrace is additive only on commuting elements
Claim: an algebra where every quasitrace misses additivity by at least $1/144$

achievement.label: Kaplansky's quasitrace question
statement: \text{every 2-quasitrace on a C*-algebra is a trace}
achievement.context: Before: yes for exact algebras (Haagerup, circulated 1991); this algebra is non-exact
achievement.note: Also: two stably finite algebras with a properly infinite tensor product

verify.detail: Both statements, with the $1/144$ in the statement itself
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.ref: article, Kaplansky's quasitraces are not traces
sources.quote: with the $1/144$ in the statement itself

plain: A quasitrace measures size but adds up correctly only for pieces that commute; here it can never fully add up

steps: A quasitrace adds up correctly only on commuting pieces
Build an algebra with two pieces where adding always fails
Every quasitrace misses by at least $1/144$: no trace exists

data.label: misses by at least $1/144$
data.caption: commuting pairs add up; one pair never does

voice.text: A quasitrace adds up correctly only on commuting elements.
Kaplansky asked whether it always adds.
Build an algebra where adding always fails, by at least one hundred forty-fourth.
Claimed: so no tracial state exists.
